10: # Presentation
11: 
12: Turn a technical specification into an interactive, persuasive web deck —
13: the kind at iii.dev/roadmap/. The output is a **content layer** inside the
14: repo's roadmap base (the shared component library, gallery, and markdown
15: spec viewer that build every deck into one static site — Astro routes of the
16: site package in iii, a standalone Vite project in other repos):
17: 
18: 1. helps engineers **understand** the spec — the architecture is a navigable
19:    map, not prose;
20: 2. is **interactive** — steppable diagrams, a selectable system map, live
21:    toggles; interactivity is what makes it stick;
22: 3. reads like **marketing** — it argues the *why*. if no one is convinced the
23:    work should happen, the spec has not done its job;
24: 4. is **build-in-public ready** — each deck ships as a static page at
25:    `/roadmap/<slug>/`, safe to share.
26: 
27: ## Comparable to
28: 
29: A product launch microsite generated from an RFC. Stripe-doc clarity meets a
30: keynote narrative, in a monospace drafting-sheet style.
31: 
32: ## Activation
33: 
34: ### Use For
35: 
36: - generating an interactive deck from a tech-spec directory
37: - refreshing or extending a presentation already generated by this skill
38: 
39: ### Do Not Use For
40: 
41: - writing the spec itself — use `/tech-spec`
42: - static slide exports (pdf / keynote) — use a slide tool
43: - general UI work unrelated to a spec — use `/design`
44: 
45: ## Load First
46: 
47: Read these before building (they are the law — do not re-derive them):
48: 
49: - `reference/design-system.md` — the locked tokens, type, motion, layout
50: - `reference/archetypes.md` — the interactive slide library + how to pick one
51: - `reference/component-standards.md` — deck-local vs promoted components, the
52:   promotion checklist, the registry format
53: - `reference/narrative-framework.md` — the persuasive arc + outline rules
54: - `reference/quality-bar.md` — the checklist to self-verify before finishing
55: - `reference/hosting.md` — the two-tree layout, the pairing contract,
56:   frontmatter registration, and deploy
57: - **per repo:** `<base>/COMPONENTS.md` — the live registry of that repo's
58:   shared components. It may exceed the bundled catalog; when it and
59:   `reference/archetypes.md` disagree, **the repo registry wins**.
60: 
61: The skill bundles two scaffolds:
62: 
63: - `template/` — one deck's **content layer** (App, sections, pages, content
64:   data, the spec-docs glob). Copy it per spec; everything visual comes from the
65:   base's shared `src/` via the `@lib` alias. You generate only content.
66: - `base/` — the whole per-repo presentations site: the shared component
67:   library + design tokens, the gallery, the md-only spec viewer, and the build
68:   glue (`build.mjs`, `vite.config.ts`, one `package.json`). Copy once per repo
69:   (in iii it already lives at `website/roadmap/`); per-deck runs never
70:   modify it except **additive component promotion** per
71:   `reference/component-standards.md`.
72: 
73: ## Progress Updates
74: 
75: Emit one short line before each phase: `ingesting spec` → `reading the
76: component registry` → `proposing outline` → `scaffolding` → `generating slides
77: (k/N)` → `registering spec frontmatter` → `verifying`.
78: 
79: ## Workflow
80: 
81: Phases are gated. Do not skip Phase 2's approval or Phase 5's verification.
82: 
83: ### 0. Resolve inputs
84: 
85: - The argument is a tech-spec directory: `<repo>/tech-specs/<slug>/` —
86:   **markdown only** (README.md + domain docs; frontmatter in README.md). If
87:   given a path elsewhere, resolve into the spec tree or ask.
88: - The **slug is the spec directory's basename** (e.g. `2026-06-21-devexp` —
89:   `YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`; the day prefix orders the roadmap timeline). It is
90:   the deck directory name AND the URL segment — the pairing contract in
91:   `reference/hosting.md`. Fix it now and use it everywhere; never prettify it.
92: - Resolve the **base project**: read `<repo>/tech-specs/README.md` — the
93:   pointer names the base dir (in iii: `website/roadmap/`). Fallback:
94:   search for a dir containing both `COMPONENTS.md` and a shared `src/`.
95:   Detect its shape:
96:   - **integrated base** (shared `src/` + `scripts/manifest.mjs`, no
97:     package.json or build.mjs of its own — iii's shape: the site's Astro
98:     pages at `website/src/pages/roadmap/` render each deck's `src/App.tsx`
99:     as a React island via the base's `src/DeckHost.tsx`; deps live in the
100:     `iii-website` package) → use it, and scaffold content layers only;
101:   - **standalone base** (`build.mjs` + own `package.json`, one `index.html`
102:     per deck — the `base/` snapshot's shape) → use it;
103:   - **absent** → first run in this repo: pick the location with the user
104:     (default `website/roadmap/` when `website/` exists, else
105:     `roadmap/` at the repo root) and scaffold it in Phase 3;
106:   - **legacy layout** (`tech-specs/build.mjs` + `_gallery/` — per-deck
107:     standalone projects) → stop and offer the port procedure in
108:     `reference/hosting.md` before generating anything new.
109: - Output location is `<base>/<slug>/`. If it exists and is non-empty, ask:
110:   overwrite, update in place, or abort. **Never write a non-markdown file
111:   under `tech-specs/`.**
112: - Detect the install mode: workspace (repo `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists the
113:   base) vs standalone (`pnpm install --ignore-workspace` inside the base).
114: 
115: ### 1. Deep ingest (read, do not skim)
116: 
117: - Read the spec `README.md` in full first: thesis, architecture, principles,
118:   cross-cutting contracts, migration overview. Note whether it already has a
119:   frontmatter block (title/tagline/date/tags/status).
120: - Read every domain doc. For each, capture: the one load-bearing phrase, the
121:   pain it removes, the mechanism, any schema/fields, any sequence/lifecycle,
122:   any numbers, any honest trade-off.
123: - Build a **content inventory** (architecture, protocol/wire contract,
124:   lifecycle, state model, config schema, security, migration, …). This is the
125:   raw material for archetype matching.
126: 
127: **1b. Component awareness (before planning).** Read `<base>/COMPONENTS.md` end
128: to end and list `<base>/src/components/{schematic,diagrams}/` + `src/hooks/`.
129: The registry is the live catalog for this repo and supersedes the bundled
130: `reference/archetypes.md` where they disagree. **Reuse-first mandate:** a
131: slide may get a bespoke visual only after the catalog demonstrably has no fit
132: for its content shape. Name any planned new component in the Phase 2 outline,
133: marked `local` or `promote` (see `reference/component-standards.md`), so the
134: user approves it at the same gate.
135: 
136: ### 2. Narrative plan — THE GATE
137: 
138: - Apply the arc in `reference/narrative-framework.md`. Produce a deck outline:
139:   an ordered slide list, each with `{ title, archetype (or reused registry
140:   component), the single claim, source section(s), the concrete data it pulls,
141:   interactivity, new component: <Name> (local|promote) — only when nothing
142:   fits }`. Include candidate deep-dive pages.
143: - Derive the hero line + three-value subhead + stat strip. Choose the wordmark
144:   label.
145: - **Present the outline to the user for approval/edits before scaffolding.**
146:   This is the cheapest place to turn a dry spec into a story. Skip only if the
147:   user explicitly says "just build it".
148: 
149: ### 3. Scaffold (mechanical)
150: 
151: **The deck:**
152: 
153: - `mkdir -p <base>/<slug>/` and copy `template/` into it — in an
154:   **integrated base (iii)** copy `template/src/` only and skip `index.html`
155:   and `src/main.tsx` (the site's `[slug]/index.astro` route provides the
156:   document shell and mounts `src/App.tsx`; the page title/description come
157:   from the spec frontmatter).
158: - Substitute the `__SPEC_MD_GLOB__` literal in `src/spec-docs.ts` with the
159:   computed relative path from `<base>/<slug>/src/` to
160:   `<specs-dir>/<slug>/*.md` (in iii: `../../../../tech-specs/<slug>/*.md`);
161:   in a standalone base also `__TITLE__` / `__DESCRIPTION__` in `index.html`.
162: - **No per-deck install, no per-deck config, no lockfile.** Ensure deps once:
163:   workspace mode → `pnpm install` at the repo root (only if the base's deps
164:   are missing); standalone mode → `pnpm install --ignore-workspace` in
165:   `<base>` (commit the generated lockfile).
166: 
167: **Registration:** write or update the YAML frontmatter block at the top of
168: `tech-specs/<slug>/README.md` (schema in `reference/hosting.md`): title +
169: tagline from the approved hero, `date: YYYY-MM-DD` (day precision — the
170: roadmap timeline orders and labels by it), 0–4 tags, `status: draft`.
171: There is no central manifest — the build aggregates every spec's frontmatter,
172: so this run touches nothing shared. If frontmatter already exists, update only
173: the fields this run owns (tagline polish, status).
174: 
175: **The base project** (first run in a repo only): copy `base/` into the chosen
176: dir (never its `node_modules`/`dist`). Fill the identity once: `__REPO__` in
177: `package.json`; the `__GALLERY_*__` / `__WORDMARK_LABEL__` / `__HERO_*__` /
178: `__ATTRIBUTION__` / `__SITE_HOST__` tokens in `index.html`,
179: `src/gallery/site.ts`, and `README.md`; write the `tech-specs/README.md`
180: pointer. The gallery page is a **roadmap**: hero copy in roadmap voice
181: (`__HERO_TITLE__` ≈ "what we're working on"; `__HERO_LEAD__` hints at the
182: current priority and what already landed, without naming specs), and the spec
183: list renders as a one-column timeline, newest first, grouped by month. In a workspace repo, add the base to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` **with
184: user confirmation** (a repo-level file). Never touch `build.mjs`,
185: `vite.config.ts`, tsconfigs, or `src/` beyond this copy.
186: 
187: ### 4. Generate the content layer
188: 
189: Edit only these — the write surface is `<base>/<slug>/**` plus the spec's
190: frontmatter block (and an approved promotion):
191: 
192: - `src/content/deck.ts` — `DECK_META.wordmarkLabel`, `NAV`, `FOOTER`.
193: - `src/content/<topic>.ts` — the typed data arrays each archetype consumes
194:   (map nodes/edges/info, sequence lanes/steps, reveal stages, cli tracks,
195:   metrics, rows). Keep data here, out of components.
196: - `src/sections/<Name>.tsx` — one thin section per slide: import the matching
197:   archetype from `@lib`, feed it data, wrap it in `<Section>`. Replace the
198:   example sections; delete `src/content/example.ts` and `pages/ExamplePage.tsx`.
199: - `src/pages/<Name>.tsx` — deep dives via `@lib` `<PageShell>`.
200: - `src/App.tsx` — wire the ordered `SECTIONS` array and the `PAGES` map.
201: 
202: **The component protocol** (when a load-bearing concept has no fit in
203: `COMPONENTS.md`):
204: 
205: 1. **Default: build it deck-local** in `<base>/<slug>/src/diagrams/<Name>.tsx`,
206:    following `@lib/components/diagrams/SequencePlayer.tsx` conventions.
207: 2. **Promote into `<base>/src/components/` only when all three hold:** (a) it
208:    is generic over its data — nothing spec-specific inside, everything arrives
209:    via typed props; (b) it maps to a recurring spec shape (a lifecycle, a
210:    tree, a timeline, a fan-out…) future decks will plausibly need; (c) it
211:    passes the checklist in `reference/component-standards.md` without
212:    deck-specific hacks.
213: 3. A promotion = the component file **plus its `COMPONENTS.md` entry in the
214:    same change**. An unregistered shared component is a defect (the base's
215:    registry check warns — `scripts/validate-roadmap.ts` in iii, `build.mjs`
216:    standalone; strict mode makes it fatal).
217: 4. Never fork a shared component into the deck to tweak it — extend it via
218:    additive, non-breaking props, or build a genuinely different deck-local
219:    one. **Modifying an existing shared component requires explicit user
220:    approval** (it re-renders every other deck).
221: 
222: **Built-in spec viewer — do not delete.** Every deck ships the `#/spec` page:
223: the template wires `spec-docs.ts` (the compile-time glob over the paired
224: spec's markdown) into `@lib/pages/SpecPage` via `PAGES.spec`, and the shared
225: `TopNav` renders the `spec` link. The shared markdown renderer strips the
226: frontmatter block. It needs no per-deck content — leave the wiring in place.
227: 
228: ### 5. Verify — THE SECOND GATE
229: 
230: All commands run from `<base>`'s package (iii: `pnpm --filter iii-website
231: <script>` from the repo root; standalone: inside `<base>`):
232: 
233: - `pnpm type-check` — the whole roadmap project (shared src + gallery + every
234:   deck) must pass strict; fix every error.
235: - The build must succeed with zero frontmatter-validation or registry-parity
236:   warnings — iii: `pnpm build` (the site build runs the roadmap contract
237:   checks and emits `dist/roadmap/<slug>/`); standalone: `node build.mjs
238:   --only=<slug>`.
239: - `pnpm dev` in the background, then dogfood with the **`/browse` skill**
240:   (never `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`): load
241:   `http://localhost:4321/roadmap/<slug>/` (standalone: `:5173/<slug>/`),
242:   click the map, run a stepper, toggle the theme, open a deep-dive, open
243:   `#/spec` and confirm every markdown file renders (mermaid fences live, no
244:   raw frontmatter). Zero console errors; no horizontal body scroll at 375px.
245: - `pnpm build && pnpm preview`, then `/browse
246:   http://localhost:4321/roadmap/` (standalone: `:4173/`): the spec appears on
247:   the roadmap timeline in date order under its month, its card shows the
248:   frontmatter title/tagline/tags with the day marker in the timeline gutter,
249:   and clicking it lands on `/roadmap/<slug>/`. If the spec previously served
250:   the md-only viewer, confirm the deck replaced it at the same URL.
251: - **If anything under `<base>/src/` was touched (a promotion): run the full
252:   site build** — a shared change must not break sibling decks.
253: - Run `reference/quality-bar.md` end to end; fix anything red.
254: 
255: ### 6. Hand off
256: 
257: Report: the deck path (`<base>/<slug>/`), the dev URL, the slide list, which
258: interactions are live, the frontmatter written, and any promoted components
259: (with their registry entries). Offer to flip `status: draft` → `live`.
260: Deploy is not a step: **in iii, merging to main ships everything via
261: `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml` to `iii.dev/roadmap/<slug>/`**; in
262: other repos `dist/` is a portable static site for whatever CI they use. Do
263: **not** commit, push, or configure hosting unless asked. Never run `vercel`.
264: 
265: ## Rules
266: 
267: - **The shared layer is law**: never edit `<base>/src/**`, the base's build
268:   glue (iii: `website/src/pages/roadmap/` and `scripts/validate-roadmap.ts`;
269:   standalone: `build.mjs` and `vite.config.ts`), tsconfigs, `package.json`,
270:   or the gallery in a deck run.
271:   Sole exception: additive component promotion under
272:   `reference/component-standards.md`, always paired with a `COMPONENTS.md`
273:   entry.
274: - A deck run's write surface is `<base>/<slug>/**` plus the frontmatter block
275:   of `tech-specs/<slug>/README.md`. Nothing else.
276: - `tech-specs/` holds markdown only. Never write a non-md file there; never

278: - Reuse first: consult `COMPONENTS.md` before building any visual; the repo

284: - Ration the accent (success / active / CTA only). Lowercase copy; identifiers
285:   keep their casing. No em-dashes. No "robust / comprehensive / crucial /
286:   seamless / unlock".
287: - Ground every claim in the spec. Keep one honest trade-offs/open-questions
288:   beat — honesty reads as credibility.
289: - Quantify the win: use the spec's numbers verbatim; if you compute one, say so.
